content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text uses Matthew 1:20's competing answers as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED, which is exactly the kind of ruling K-S2 governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.", "room": "'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.' I weighed (1) the judge's treatment of 'covenant presence' and 'physical source in the womb' as two senses making Matthew 1:20 open/UNDERDETERMINED, against (2) K-S2's reading that such a dual-sense verse is not open and both senses stand.", "why": "The judge says UNDERDETERMINED because Matthew 1:20 was answered as covenant presence and as physical source in the womb, which treats the verse as open despite K-S2's command that both senses stand."}
